functions.description: Extract the amount of gas in moles, the volume with its unit, the temperature with its unit, and the gas name from the problem parameters.
inputs: the amount of gas n with unit and chemical formula of the gas species and its physical state
the volume V occupied by the gas with its unit
the temperature T of the gas with its unit
the name of the gas species whose pressure is to be predicted
outputs: amount of gas n in moles

functions.description: Convert a temperature in degrees Celsius to kelvin by adding 273.15
inputs: temperature in degrees Celsius

functions.description: Convert a volume given with its unit, such as dm3, L or cm3, into cubic metres.
inputs: volume with its unit

functions.description: Convert a temperature to kelvin and a volume to cubic metres so that both are in SI units.
inputs: temperature with its unit
volume with its unit

functions.description: Compute the pressure of a perfect gas from p = nRT/V using SI units, giving the result in pascals.
inputs: amount of gas n in moles
absolute temperature in kelvin
volume in cubic metres

functions.description: Convert a pressure in pascals to atmospheres, bar and megapascals.
inputs: perfect gas pressure in pascals

functions.description: Cross-check a perfect gas pressure by recomputing p = nRT/V in atm with R = 0.082057 dm3 atm K-1 mol-1 and the volume in cubic decimetres.
inputs: amount of gas n in moles
absolute temperature in kelvin
volume with its unit

functions.description: Compare two pressure values expressed in atmospheres to confirm that they agree within rounding
inputs: pressure in atmospheres from the SI calculation
cross-checked pressure in atmospheres

functions.description: Predict the pressure exerted by a perfect gas confined to a given volume at a given temperature from the perfect gas equation.
inputs: the amount of gas n with unit and chemical formula of the gas species and its physical state
the volume V occupied by the gas with its unit
the temperature T of the gas with its unit
the name of the gas species whose pressure is to be predicted
outputs: predicted pressure of the gas with its unit in pascals, atmospheres and megapascals

entry_points.text: Suppose that ●1 is confined to ●2 at ●3. Predict the pressure exerted by the ●4 from the perfect gas equation.

params.description: the amount of gas n with unit and chemical formula of the gas species and its physical state
params.validity_range: The amount must be a positive finite number of moles (n > 0). The species must be a gaseous substance under the stated conditions so that the perfect gas equation applies; the stated state (g) must be consistent with the temperature and pressure of the system.

params.description: the volume V occupied by the gas with its unit
params.validity_range: The volume must be a positive finite quantity (V > 0) with a unit of volume that can be converted to cubic metres. Very small volumes at which the gas would condense or molecular volume becomes significant violate the perfect gas assumption.

params.description: the temperature T of the gas with its unit
params.validity_range: The temperature must be above absolute zero, i.e. above -273.15°C or greater than 0 K (T > 0 K), and it must be a temperature at which the substance is a gas. Very low temperatures near condensation invalidate the perfect gas model.

params.description: the name of the gas species whose pressure is to be predicted
params.validity_range: Must name a single gaseous substance that can be treated as a perfect gas under the stated conditions and whose amount is given by ●1. Names of substances that are liquid or solid at the stated temperature are outside the class, since the perfect gas equation would not apply.
